claims.text: Missed appointments are a network-wide problem: 18.4% of 41,200 bookings were no-shows, with every clinic between 15% and 22%.
No-shows drive course drop-off: 34% of patients stop before session 4, and 71% of them missed an appointment first.
Patients who drop off mostly do so because nobody explained what the full course is for.
Reminders with one-tap rescheduling roughly halve no-shows (18.9% to 9.7% in a randomized pilot).
Automating confirmations will free about 90 minutes of front-desk time per clinic per day, the task staff most want removed.
Network-wide reminders are likely worth around 7,900 recovered appointments (≈£380k) a year, based on the finance model.
Roll out SMS reminders with one-tap rescheduling to all 14 clinics, integrated with ClinicDesk.
Add a clinician-approved 'why your course matters' message after session 1 to address drop-off.
Home-exercise reminders by SMS are likely to help completion, but the evidence comes from other settings and a preference survey.
Older patients hesitated at the date picker; accessibility should be watched as rollout widens.
The revenue estimate may not hold if pilot clinics differ from the rest of the network.

gaps.missing: Evidence that the session-1 education message reduces drop-off
gaps.why_it_matters: It is the main lever for drop-off but is untested
gaps.would_raise_confidence: A/B test across 2–3 clinics measuring completion past session 4
